input.strategy_title: Graduate Llama Stack to General Availability
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Llama Stack shipped as Tech Preview and adoption is strong, but enterprise
customers will not build production GenAI applications on a TP component.
Graduating to GA requires API stability commitments, a production support
posture, and closing the quality gaps that TP status currently excuses. The
full inventory of those gaps is not yet known — TP feedback is scattered across
support tickets, and no systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases. |
| HLR-3 | P0 | Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. |
| HLR-5 | P1 | The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). |
| HLR-6 | P2 | Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including migration notes from TP. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- TrustyAI
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- New Llama Stack feature development beyond GA-bar quality work
- Deprecating alternative GenAI serving paths

## Open Questions

1. The GA scope itself depends on HLR-1's assessment — until it lands, the
   size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate.

# GA-Readiness Assessment Producing the Definitive GA Scope

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's central unknown: the full inventory of gaps
between Llama Stack's current Tech Preview quality and the General
Availability bar. It systematically consolidates TP feedback scattered across
support tickets, architecture context, and the platform's GA criteria, and
produces the definitive GA scope that all downstream stability, hardening, and
support-posture work is planned against.

## Scope

- Collect and triage Tech Preview feedback from support tickets, issue
  trackers, and known-issues records for the Llama Stack component.
- Assess current state against the GA bar in the four dimensions named by the
  strategy: API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and error handling.
- Produce a GA-readiness report: a gap inventory with severity, affected
  surfaces, and recommended disposition for each gap.
- Produce the definitive GA scope document: which gaps are in scope for GA,
  deferred, or accepted with documented limitations.
- Flag any gap whose remediation would require work beyond the stability and
  support-posture streams (e.g. substantial error-handling or scale-limit
  rework) so the epic plan can be revisited.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A GA-readiness report exists that inventories gaps across API stability,
  upgrade paths, scale limits, and error handling, with each gap traceable to
  its feedback source.
- Every gap in the inventory has a disposition: in GA scope, deferred, or
  accepted-with-limitation.
- The definitive GA scope document is published and agreed with stakeholders,
  such that downstream stability and support-posture work can be sized against
  it rather than estimated.
- Feedback sources consulted are listed in the report, covering the support
  ticket record of the Tech Preview period.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP
  quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error
  handling), producing the definitive GA scope — this epic is that assessment.

# Llama Stack API Stability Guarantee: Versioned APIs, Deprecation Policy, Tested Upgrade Path

## Description

This epic puts a stability guarantee on Llama Stack's published API surface so
enterprise customers can build production GenAI applications against it. It
delivers versioned APIs, a published deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade
path from the last two Tech Preview releases, plus remediation of the
API-stability and upgrade-path gaps that the GA-readiness assessment
identifies and dispositions into GA scope. The epic is gated by the
GA-readiness assessment: its findings determine which surfaces must be
stabilized and how much hardening work is in scope.

## Scope

- Introduce API versioning on the published Llama Stack API surface (the
  OpenAI-compatible REST APIs and the LlamaStackDistribution CRD surface).
- Define and publish a deprecation policy covering how API changes are
  versioned, announced, and retired.
- Build and test an upgrade path from the last two Tech Preview releases to
  the GA release, including migration of existing LlamaStackDistribution
  custom resources.
- Remediate the API-stability and upgrade-path gaps inventoried by the
  GA-readiness assessment that are dispositioned into GA scope.
- Ensure the component's existing Konflux build pipeline remains green for
  all changes in this epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published APIs carry explicit version identifiers, and the versioning scheme
  is documented.
- A deprecation policy is published describing versioning, notice periods,
  and removal rules for API changes.
- An automated or repeatable upgrade test demonstrates successful upgrade from
  each of the last two Tech Preview releases to the GA release, including
  preservation of existing distribution custom resources.
- Every API-stability and upgrade-path gap from the GA-readiness assessment
  that was dispositioned into GA scope is remediated or explicitly accepted
  with a documented limitation.
- The Konflux build pipeline for the Llama Stack component is green with the
  changes in this epic.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned
  APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP
  releases.
- HLR-1 (P0, partial): remediation of the assessment-inventoried
  API-stability and upgrade-path gaps dispositioned into GA scope on the
  API surface. Error-handling and scale-limit remediation is not in this
  epic's committed scope; if the assessment surfaces such gaps, they are
  absorbed via the GA-readiness gate's rewrite/spawn semantics.

# Llama Stack Production Support Posture: SLO Targets, Backport Policy, Supported Configuration Matrix

## Description

This epic establishes the production support posture required for General
Availability of Llama Stack: documented SLO targets, a backport policy, and a
supported configuration matrix. It turns the Tech Preview "best effort"
posture into defined, publishable support commitments, informed by the
scale-limit and error-handling findings of the GA-readiness assessment.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the Llama Stack component in production
  deployments (informed by the assessment's scale-limit findings).
- Define and document a backport policy: which releases receive fixes, for how
  long, and how backports are delivered.
- Define and publish a supported configuration matrix: the provider plugins,
  inference providers, vector/RAG providers, and deployment topologies that
  are supported and tested at GA.
- Capture support-commitment content in the appropriate product
  documentation/policy locations, aligned with the platform's existing
  support-posture conventions for GA components.
- Fold in any support-posture gaps the GA-readiness assessment dispositions
  into GA scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documented SLO targets exist and are published for the GA release.
- A backport policy is published stating supported release windows and
  backport delivery mechanics.
- A supported configuration matrix is published listing the tested, supported
  provider and deployment combinations, with unsupported combinations
  explicitly marked.
- Every support-posture gap from the GA-readiness assessment dispositioned
  into GA scope is addressed or explicitly accepted with a documented
  limitation.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P0): Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets,
  backport policy, and supported configuration matrix.
- HLR-1 (P0, partial): scale-limit and error-handling findings from the
  assessment feed the SLO targets and configuration matrix.

# TrustyAI Guardrails as a Supported, Documented Llama Stack Integration

## Description

This epic promotes the TrustyAI safety-guardrails integration for Llama Stack
from an experimental flag to a supported, documented integration in GA
distributions. The TrustyAI team owns the integration work on the TrustyAI
side and authors the technical documentation of the integration as a
supported configuration; publication of that content in the GA documentation
set at GA standard is owned by the documentation uplift work that depends on
this epic.

## Scope

- Promote the guardrails integration from experimental/opt-in status to a
  supported integration for GA Llama Stack distributions.
- Validate that the integration works against the published, versioned,
  stability-guaranteed Llama Stack API surface (the OpenAI-compatible REST
  APIs and provider-plugin model), so the supported integration targets the
  GA API rather than TP-era behavior.
- Harden the integration to supported quality: error handling, failure
  modes, and configuration validation appropriate for a supported
  integration.
- Document the integration: supported deployment topology, configuration
  steps, and support boundaries between the TrustyAI and Llama Stack
  components. This epic authors the technical content for the integration;
  uplifting that content into the published GA documentation set at GA
  standard is owned separately by the documentation uplift work, which
  consumes this content as an input.
- Ensure the TrustyAI component's existing Konflux build pipeline remains
  green for changes in this epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Enabling TrustyAI guardrails on a GA Llama Stack distribution no longer
  requires an experimental flag, and the integration is listed as a supported
  configuration.
- The integration is validated against the versioned GA API surface, including
  behavior when the API signals deprecation.
- Documentation exists describing how to deploy, configure, and troubleshoot
  the guardrails integration, including the support boundary between the two
  components.
- The Konflux build pipeline for the TrustyAI component is green with the
  changes in this epic.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions.

# Dashboard: Enable Llama Stack Management by Default for Entitled Clusters

## Description

This epic removes the Tech Preview opt-in gate for Llama Stack management in
the Dashboard, so that Llama Stack management is enabled by default for
entitled clusters at GA. The Dashboard owns the feature-flag default and the
user-facing management experience.

## Scope

- Change the Llama Stack management feature flag from an opt-in (Tech Preview
  gate) to enabled-by-default for entitled clusters, following the Dashboard's
  existing per-component feature-flag and defaults mechanism.
- Verify the Llama Stack management experience (navigation section, resource
  views, and any creation/status surfaces the Dashboard already ships for
  Llama Stack) works correctly when enabled by default.
- Handle entitlement gating: default-on applies only to entitled clusters;
  non-entitled clusters must not see Llama Stack management.
- Update Dashboard feature-flag documentation/defaults references that fall
  out of this change.
- Ensure the Dashboard component's existing Konflux build pipeline remains
  green for changes in this epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On an entitled cluster with default configuration (no opt-in set), Llama
  Stack management is available in the Dashboard with no manual feature-flag
  change.
- On a non-entitled cluster, Llama Stack management remains hidden.
- Existing opt-in configurations continue to work (no regression for clusters
  that explicitly enabled the feature during Tech Preview).
- The Dashboard's automated test suite covers the default-on entitlement
  behavior and passes.
- The Konflux build pipeline for the Dashboard component is green with the
  changes in this epic.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P1): The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for
  entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate).

# Llama Stack GA Documentation Uplift with TP Migration Notes

## Description

This epic uplifts Llama Stack documentation to GA standards and provides
migration notes from Tech Preview, so that customers moving production
workloads onto the GA release have accurate, complete documentation. It is
authored after the implementation work lands, because the documentation
describes what was built.

## Scope

Content outline (to be finalized against the delivered GA scope):

- GA-ready product documentation for Llama Stack: installation/configuration,
  the versioned API surface and its stability guarantee, and the deprecation
  policy.
- Migration notes from Tech Preview: upgrading from the last two TP releases,
  migrating existing LlamaStackDistribution custom resources, and behavior
  changes between TP and GA.
- Supported configuration matrix, SLO targets, and backport policy as
  customer-facing documentation.
- The TrustyAI guardrails integration documented as a supported configuration,
  including its support boundary. The TrustyAI team authors this technical
  content (deployment topology, configuration, troubleshooting) as part of the
  integration work; this epic's ownership is uplifting that content into the
  published GA documentation set at GA standard.
- Dashboard default enablement for entitled clusters reflected in
  documentation (removal of the TP opt-in instructions).
- Removal or correction of Tech Preview caveats and disclaimers that no
  longer apply at GA.

## Acceptance Criteria
